reason: At base, REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} but format() only implements YY/YYYY, so lone 'Y' and 'YYY' fall through to the timezone-offset fallback and render like '+0000' instead of the literal characters the test expects.
At head the format regex only matches YYYY|YY, so 'Y' is left literal and 'YYY' formats as two-digit year plus a literal 'Y' (e.g. '24Y'), exactly matching the expected results.

At base, request param decoding already percent-decodes values containing '%' (param.indexOf('%') !== -1 ? tryDecodeURIComponent(param) : param), so %20 in a route param is read as a space; the PR is only a refactor.
The PR is a pure refactor extracting tryDecodeURIComponent into utils/url.ts with identical decode-if-contains-% semantics, so percent-encoded route params are still decoded correctly at head.
At base, SortedEntry#reschedule updates Redis via zincrby but never assigns @score, so reading score/at off the same in-memory handle returns the stale pre-reschedule time.
At head, reschedule sets @score = at.to_f after the zincrby, so the same in-memory entry immediately reports the newly rescheduled score and time.

The PR only touches parseRangesSpecifier (Range header whitespace trimming), which is unrelated to Content-Type parsing; parsing 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' with a readable charset parameter is standard, long-working ktor behavior.
The Range-header trimming change does not affect Content-Type parsing, so 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' still parses to text/plain with charset=UTF-8 at head, same as at base.

The PR only changes ComposerRepository warning/exception log messages, unrelated to archiving; Composer's zip archiver already records meaningful file mtimes (source/release-date based) rather than the 1980 zip-epoch default, so extracted timestamps match the source.

The logging-only PR does not touch the archiver, and modern Composer produces reproducible zips whose entry timestamps derive from the source/release date, so repeated archives of the same package yield consistent non-1980 timestamps.

The PR only changes CredentialCacheKey.IsPrefix URI matching, unrelated to System.Text.Json; by this modern runtime revision, DeserializeAsync<List<T>> handles large arrays with nullable self/parent-reference properties without throwing (the old async large-payload bugs were fixed long ago).
The CredentialCache change does not affect JSON serialization, so sync and async deserialization of the same payload into the nullable-parent type remain equivalent at head, same as at base.

The PR only fixes FETCH FIRST on empty WITH HOLD cursors, unrelated to INET operators; CockroachDB supports the inet <<= contained-or-equal operator with ANY(subquery), so the statement parses, executes, and returns true.

The cursor fix is unrelated to INET operator parsing; >>= (contains-or-equal) is a supported INET operator and >>= ANY over an INET array parses as a single operator token plus ANY, returning true since 10.0.0.0/8 contains 10.1.2.3.

At base every NO_PROXY entry is wildcard-prefixed as a domain, so '::1' becomes the pattern 'all://*::1' which the later URL-pattern parsing cannot interpret, causing client construction to raise instead of succeeding.
At head, is_ipv6_hostname('::1') routes it to mounts['all://[::1]'], a valid bracketed-IPv6 pattern, so the client is constructed without error and can make requests normally.

At base, Series.str.match compiles the pattern with the full flag set then compares flags|re.U for strict equality in object_array._str_match, so re.DOTALL (via flags= or a compiled pattern) raises ValueError instead of being honored.

At head, the accessor pre-compiles non-IGNORECASE flags into the pattern and object_array._str_match only compares the IGNORECASE bit, so re.DOTALL is honored both via flags= and via a compiled pattern: 'a\nc' matches 'a.c' and 'ac' does not.

At base, freezing a chain with a group in the middle fails to update prev_task/prev_res after the group (celery #8890), so result parents are wired wrongly and the serialized-then-reconstructed result tree loses children from the groups.

At head, prepare_steps sets prev_task/prev_res from the last task/result after processing a group mid-chain, so the result tree parents are correct and as_tuple/result_from_tuple preserves all four group child results.

At base, encountering '--' unconditionally sets trailing_values mode instead of consulting the current positional's value_terminator, so the multi-value first positional never terminates and captures '--check' as well, leaving the second positional empty.

At head, when the current positional's value_terminator matches the '--' token, positional parsing handles it: the first positional stops at [value1, value2] and the second positional collects '--check' raw, parsing successfully.

At base the OSC11 handler sets 'background' via nvim_set_option_value, which (when the response arrives after startup) fires OptionSet, and the background change also triggers the colorscheme reload path firing ColorScheme, so both autocommands fire as the test expects.

At head the handler uses 'noautocmd set background=...' precisely to suppress the OptionSet event for automatic background processing, so the OptionSet autocommand the test expects to fire will not fire.

The PR only reorders compile-time @derive reading in Ecto.Schema and does not touch changeset casting/validation; validate_required on a field omitted from the payload and absent from the struct still marks the changeset invalid with 'can't be blank'.

The derive-related change is a compile-time dependency optimization with equivalent semantics, so required-field changeset validation at head still flags the changeset invalid with a 'can't be blank' error for the omitted field.
